minor_characters.name: Mr. Chadband
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A windbag preacher who harangues Jo at Mr. Snagsby’s, intrudes at the Sol’s Arms, and delivers long sermons (‘Nurse and Patient,’ ‘The Appointed Time’ setup)
minor_characters.reason_removable: His comic-sermonizing adds satire but does not affect Jo’s fate, Lady Dedlock’s secret, Bucket’s case, or Esther’s arc and can be cut or greatly condensed.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Chadband
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Grim spouse who stages Chadband’s platforms and appears in their scenes with the Snagsbys and at the Sol’s Arms
minor_characters.reason_removable: She only amplifies the Chadband satire and has no plot agency; cutting her with Chadband trims dead weight.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Quale
minor_characters.appearances_summary: A syrupy ‘mission’ man who flatters every cause, attends Jellyby/Pardiggle circles, and appears at Caddy’s wedding breakfast
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is a satirical type with no bearing on Esther, the Dedlocks, Jo, or the case; all his business can be excised.

minor_characters.name: Miss Wisk
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Militant ‘woman’s mission’ guest, sparring at Caddy’s wedding breakfast
minor_characters.reason_removable: Pure social satire not needed for the main story; removing her does not change any character’s decisions or outcomes.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Pardiggle
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Long-waistcoated bass-voiced husband dragged in Mrs. Pardiggle’s charity train and present at the wedding breakfast
minor_characters.reason_removable: He is scenery for philanthropic mockery and has no effect on Jo, Esther, or the Dedlocks.

minor_characters.name: Pardiggle boys (Egbert, Oswald, Francis, Felix, Alfred)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: One-note comic terrors brandished as ‘mites’ in Mrs. Pardiggle’s scenes
minor_characters.reason_removable: They serve only to burlesque their mother and can be removed with her without loss to plot or themes already covered by Jellyby.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Piper & Mrs. Perkins
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Gossipy court neighbours outside Krook’s shop (Sol’s Arms nights), recurring as local colour
minor_characters.reason_removable: Their chatter is atmospheric only; cutting them leaves Krook’s death, Bucket, and Weevle/Jobling intact.

minor_characters.name: Little Swills and Miss M. Melvilleson (‘the noted siren’)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Harmonic meeting performers at the Sol’s Arms
minor_characters.reason_removable: Comic tavern texture not needed for any causal beat; Krook’s plot proceeds without their interludes.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Badger & Mrs. Bayham Badger
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Elderly medical couple who introduce Allan Woodcourt and talk genealogies and past husbands
minor_characters.reason_removable: Woodcourt can be introduced directly; their long genealogical patter is expendable without harming Esther–Allan or the themes.

minor_characters.name: Mr. and Mrs. Bagnet (and Quebec, Malta, and Woolwich)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: George’s warm-hearted military friends who host him and Guppy and bolster later support
minor_characters.reason_removable: Their domestic set-pieces are detachable; George’s arc (debt, Smallweeds, Dedlocks) reads without their family scenes.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Snagsby
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Jealous, suspicious wife whose ‘sees it all’ subplot has her shadowing and misconstruing Jo/Snagsby/Bucket
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her jealousy never affects Jo’s capture, Tulkinghorn’s murder, or Bucket’s solution and can be omitted.

minor_characters.name: Volumnia Dedlock
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Fashionable cousin used for small-talk and to pad Chesney Wold social scenes (and later to flutter about appearances)
minor_characters.reason_removable: If the ending still notes ‘Volumnia flutters to keep up appearances,’ earlier chatter-scenes can be dropped wholesale.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Bogsby (landlord of the Sol’s Arms)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapter 034; presides over the tavern crowd after Krook’s combustion, sells drinks, and hosts comic ‘Harmonic’ evenings.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Provides local colour and satire of sensation-seeking crowds but does not affect the investigation, Lady Dedlock’s arc, Richard’s fate, or Esther’s story.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Swills and Miss M. Melvilleson (Harmonic performers)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapter 034; tavern-singer and lady vocalist used for comic set‑pieces about the ‘popular song’ and mock-bills.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Purely comic atmosphere pieces; cutting them does not change any plot turn or theme.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Piper and Mrs. Perkins (Chancery Lane neighbours)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapter 034; gossiping neighbours who add to the crowd narrative after Krook’s death.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Peripheral commentators who do not influence events or characters.

minor_characters.name: Mrs. Guppy (Mr. Guppy’s mother)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapters 039 and 063; appears in comic interruptions during Guppy’s renewed proposals and at Kenge’s office.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Her scenes are broad comedy that can be summarized or dropped without affecting Esther’s decisions or the legal outcome.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Weevle/Mr. Jobling
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapters 039 and 063; Guppy’s friend who shadows tavern gossip and later tags along to Kenge’s office.
minor_characters.reason_removable: In these late chapters he contributes only comic asides and can be excised without loss to the main mysteries.

minor_characters.name: Mr. Sladdery (fashion librarian/society purveyor)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapter 041; lampoons ‘high connexion’ and how rumors spread.
minor_characters.reason_removable: A one‑scene satire of fashion-trade gossip that does not touch the Dedlock secret or the suit.

minor_characters.name: Mercury (Dedlock footman)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapters 041, 043, and 054; recurring nameless footman figure used for doors and messages.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Household business that can be implied in narration; dropping him changes nothing.

minor_characters.name: Old Mr. Turveydrop (epilogue mention)
minor_characters.appearances_summary: Chapter 062; a brief update that he ‘exhibits deportment’ and patronizes Peepy.
minor_characters.reason_removable: Epilogue colour only; removing his update does not affect the resolution of any central character.

subplots.name: Chadband’s sermons and Jo’s coerced ‘improvement’
subplots.reason_removable: Lengthy comic-ecclesiastical set-pieces add satire but do not change Jo’s trajectory, Bucket’s inquiry, or the Dedlock secret; Jo’s persecution and kindness can be shown via Snagsby/Bucket without Chadband.

subplots.name: Mrs. Snagsby’s jealousy investigation (‘sees it all’)
subplots.reason_removable: Her sleuthing never intersects with Bucket’s case or alters Jo’s fate; excising it removes noise without touching the plot spine.

subplots.name: Mr. Quale/Miss Wisk mission-salon orbit
subplots.reason_removable: Redundant to Jellyby/Pardiggle philanthropy satire; trimming them streamlines Caddy’s wedding scenes and keeps the telescopic-philanthropy theme via Mrs. Jellyby alone.

subplots.name: Sol’s Arms ‘Harmonic Meeting’ interludes
subplots.reason_removable: Tavern entertainment sequences are colour only; Krook’s spontaneous combustion and the murder plot unfold unchanged without these pauses.

subplots.name: Bagnet family domesticity
subplots.reason_removable: Warm but tangential; George’s link to Dedlock/Tulkinghorn/Smallweed and Guppy’s paper scheme read clearly without the Bagnet home scenes.

subplots.name: Miss Volumnia’s fashionable digressions with Sir Leicester
subplots.reason_removable: Earlier tittle-tattle and ‘deportment’ talk can be cut; a brief late-stage note on Volumnia ‘keeping up appearances’ suffices for the ending tableau.

subplots.name: Sol’s Arms post‑combustion carnival and press send‑ups
subplots.reason_removable: The tavern’s comic uproar and mock-newspaper flourishes satirize sensation but do not move the Bucket/Dedlock/Tulkinghorn line or the court case; a line of narration can sum it up.

subplots.name: Guppy’s renewed suit to Esther (and comic entourages)
subplots.reason_removable: Esther’s arc is already clear—she declines Guppy and later marries Woodcourt—so the repeated comic proposals and Mrs. Guppy’s scenes can be summarized in a sentence.

subplots.name: Coodle/Doodle ministerial crisis and club‑room politics
subplots.reason_removable: A stand‑alone political lampoon that neither advances Lady Dedlock’s exposure nor affects Richard’s tragedy; the novel’s class satire survives without this tour.

subplots.name: Bagnet household comedy around George’s debt call
subplots.reason_removable: George’s being squeezed by Smallweed can be kept in a few lines—much of the domestic patter at the Bagnets’ is charming but not structurally necessary to his later arrest and reconciliation.

subplots.name: Skimpole’s late‑book comic interludes and epilogue notices
subplots.reason_removable: Skimpole’s function (parasitism exposed; he exits) can be retained in a brief note when Bucket uses him and Esther later repudiates him; multiple airy conversations and his posthumous diary can be cut.

subplots.name: Volumnia’s Dedlock‑ball flourishes and later ‘soothing’ of Sir Leicester
subplots.reason_removable: Her society flutter can be folded into a sentence about the house’s hollow grandeur and Sir Leicester’s diminished state.

subplots.name: Mr. Sladdery and the ‘high connexion’ rumor mill
subplots.reason_removable: A neat satire of how gossip is manufactured, but the Lady Dedlock plot and Bucket’s work read clearly without it.

subplots.name: Epilogue mini‑updates on minor comic figures
subplots.reason_removable: Quick postscript items (e.g., Old Turveydrop, Mrs. Jellyby’s new ‘mission’) can be omitted or footnoted without disturbing the endings of Esther, Ada, George, or Sir Leicester.

digressions.reason_removable: Iconic tone-setting but largely essayistic; a tighter opening can evoke Chancery’s blight without the full panoramic excursus.

digressions.topic: Telescopic philanthropy essay before/around Mrs. Jellyby
digressions.reason_removable: Philanthropy satire can be compressed to Jellyby’s neglect and Caddy’s burden; the long taxonomic prelude stalls plot.

digressions.topic: Chesney Wold/Ghost’s Walk essaying and animal fantasia
digressions.reason_removable: Lyrical mood-piece about Dedlock grounds and beasts is descriptive rather than narrative; abridger can précis without losing the Dedlock hush.
A satirical set-piece that can be drastically shortened or dropped; Jo’s persecution and Bucket’s moves do not depend on it.

digressions.topic: Crowd-and-tavern colour around Tom-all-Alone’s and the Sol’s Arms
digressions.reason_removable: Vivid but essayistic scene-painting; Jo’s eviction and Bucket’s pursuit can be staged with fewer atmospheric detours.

digressions.topic: Mock‑newspaper reportage and tavern sociology after Krook’s combustion
digressions.reason_removable: Extended press pastiche and crowd taxonomy are satirical set‑pieces that can be condensed without harming the mystery’s momentum.

digressions.topic: Vholes’s respectability catechism and Chancery self‑business
digressions.reason_removable: Pages of deadpan legal self‑justification are thematically clear elsewhere; trimming this monologue preserves Richard’s decline while tightening pace.

digressions.topic: Ministerial flip‑flops (Coodle/Doodle), fashion‑librarian Sladdery, and club satire
digressions.reason_removable: A brilliant Dickensian aside, but largely orthogonal to Lady Dedlock’s exposure, Bucket’s pursuit, and Jarndyce and Jarndyce’s collapse.

digressions.topic: Guppy’s mother’s parlour farce and comedic by‑play
digressions.reason_removable: A broad interlude that can be summarized to retain Esther’s polite refusal without the stage‑business.
